name: SigNoz
description: Self-hosted observability for this workspace — traces, metrics and logs in one dashboard, with an OTLP endpoint any instrumented service can send to. Your own instance, your own data, no shared central collector.

volumes.reason: Path-routes this app's single public port: OTLP/HTTP's three signal paths (/v1/traces, /v1/metrics, /v1/logs) go to the otel-collector sidecar, gated by the workspace API key since this app runs with the workspace identity gate off; everything else goes to the SigNoz UI/API sidecar, which has its own login. Mounted under /etc/nginx/templates/ (not conf.d/ directly) so nginx:alpine's own entrypoint runs envsubst over it at container start, baking AW_SIGNOZ_API_KEY's live value into the generated config. See docs/architecture/aw-app-signoz.md.
Zookeeper's own metadata store for ClickHouse's replicated table engine. Without it, every container recreation loses ClickHouse's table coordination state.
All ingested traces/metrics/logs. This IS the app's data — without this volume surviving a container recreation (an update, a workspace redeploy), every restart starts from empty telemetry history.
Names a single-node cluster so SigNoz's ON CLUSTER schema migrations have a cluster to target, even though this is one ClickHouse node per workspace, not a multi-node deployment.
Caps ClickHouse's own memory usage against this sidecar's resources.mem_mb, ported from the monolith's aw-signoz setup.

SigNoz's own SQLite store — dashboards, alerts, saved views, and the admin account created via its first-run signup screen. Without this volume, a container recreation loses every dashboard and the admin account has to be recreated.

skills.description: Use this workspace's own SigNoz — the OTLP endpoint format, auth, and what's mounted where.

jwt_secret.title: Session signing secret
jwt_secret.description: Signs SigNoz's own login sessions. Ships with a default — rotate it here before relying on this instance for anything sensitive; changing it invalidates existing SigNoz sessions.

retention_days.title: Retention (days)
retention_days.description: How long ingested traces/logs/metrics are kept before ClickHouse drops them (a real ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY TTL, applied to already-stored data too — not just data ingested after this changes). Default is intentionally short so storage doesn't grow unbounded; raise it if you need a longer history.

root_account_managed.title: Manage the root account from these settings
root_account_managed.description: Off by default — a fresh install behaves exactly like today, with SigNoz's own signup screen creating the first account. Turn this on to set/reset SigNoz's root account (email + password) from this form instead: (1) it disables SigNoz's own signup screen the moment it's on, and (2) it makes the password below the source of truth — if you change the password inside SigNoz's own UI, this setting overwrites it back at the next backend restart. Nothing here validates the password before saving (see its own field); an invalid one stops the SigNoz backend from starting until you blank this switch again.

root_email.title: Root account email
root_email.description: Email for the managed root account. Only used while "Manage the root account from these settings" is on. Changing it re-points the existing root user at the new address on the next backend restart — it does not create a second account.

root_password.title: Root account password
root_password.description: At least 12 characters, with at least one lowercase letter, one uppercase letter, one digit and one symbol (from ~!@#$%^&*()_+`-={}|[]\:"<>?,./) — SigNoz's own password policy, mirrored here as documentation only. Nothing in this form currently enforces the pattern or minimum length before saving; a password that fails SigNoz's own policy will make its backend refuse to start until this is fixed. Only used while "Manage the root account from these settings" is on.

root_org_id.title: Root organization ID (advanced)
root_org_id.description: Leave this blank on a fresh install. Fill it in ONLY if this SigNoz instance already had an organization created through its own signup screen before this setting existed — set it to that organization's ID so the managed root account is applied to the SAME organization instead of silently creating a brand-new, empty one alongside it (no dashboards, no saved views, none of the telemetry already collected). Never guess or invent an ID here; look up the real one first.

signoz_api_key.title: SigNoz API key (for the query MCP tools)
signoz_api_key.description: A Personal Access Token created INSIDE SigNoz itself (open this app, then Settings → API Keys — not this workspace's own API key, which is a different credential used only for the OTLP ingest paths). Lets agents query this instance's logs/traces/metrics/alerts/dashboards through MCP tools (signoz_search_logs, signoz_aggregate_logs, and 40+ more — see the aw-signoz skill for the full list and its known gaps). Leave empty to keep those tools off — an empty value disables the upstream instead of connecting and failing every call with 401. Stored with this app's settings, so it survives updates and reinstalls.
